chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Harith ibn Muhammad Al-Ahowl, from Bureyd ibn Muawiya Al-Ijaly, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), when he intended to travel, would gather his dependents in a room, then say: 'O Allah! I entrust to You this morning my self, my wealth, my family, and my children, the present among us and the absent. O Allah! Protect us and protect upon us. O Allah! Make us in Your vicinity. O Allah! Do not deprive us of Your bounty, and do not change what is with us of Your grace and favor.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication for travelers in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith highlights the Imam’s practice of formally entrusting his household and wealth to Allah before departure, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *istiwda'* (depositing with God) as a spiritual safeguard. The supplication underscores the transient nature of worldly attachments and the reliance on divine guardianship (*jiwar*) for both the present and future states of the family. This practice serves as a model for believers to integrate mindfulness of divine protection into daily routines, particularly during transitions like travel.
